pick.mechanic_fr: Un incendie dans le marché voisin entraîne une enquête municipale et l'imposition immédiate de contrôles de sécurité et d'interdictions de travaux pour tous les établissements du quartier, y compris Le Mistral et l'appartement d'Odile.
pick.why: A new fire and mandatory inspections would reopen questions about Odile’s fire and block any quick sale or renovation, forcing the cast to act now.

draft.premise_fr: Au Mistral, Margaux demande votre commande pour la troisième fois. Gus dit que votre commande dit qui vous êtes. Il faut choisir, et dire pourquoi vous êtes encore là.
draft.setup_native: At the café Le Mistral Margaux asks your order again and wants to know why you are still staying; the group teases you. Choose your usual order and explain why you remain.
draft.objective_native: Choose your usual order (one item) and say why you are still here, in one or two short sentences.
draft.objective_semantics: Two acts: name a café order (simple noun phrase) and give a brief reason for staying (because + consequence), using a short connective (parce que / car / donc). The answer shows who you are to the group and makes your usual order a habit.
draft.causal_reason: Margaux has asked the same question twice before; Gus insists an order reveals identity, so the learner's answer will make their 'usual' order and explain their presence.

chapter.title_fr: Une commande qui dit quelque chose
chapter.dramatic_question: Quelle commande deviendra la vôtre, et pourquoi restez-vous ici ?
possible_developments: The learner's order becomes their 'usual order' and Gus announces them as habitué.
Someone remembers the learner differently, causing a small surprise.
A consequence: the learner's reason raises a practical question about the succession.

panels.narration_fr: Le Mistral, soirée pluvieuse. Gus commente pendant que Lila rit.

dialogue.text_fr: Règle numéro un : l'ordre révèle l'âme.
dialogue.text_native: Rule number one: the order reveals the soul.

dialogue.text_fr: Sept sur vingt si tu prends toujours la même chose.
dialogue.text_native: Seven out of twenty if you always take the same thing.

panels.visual_direction: Wide shot of the zinc counter: Margaux behind the bar, Gus in the booth making a show, Lila perched on a stool, Romy holding a small notebook. Rain on the window behind them.
panels.alt_native: Interior of the café with people at the zinc and rain outside.

dialogue.text_fr: Oui, la même chose. On saura qui tu es.
dialogue.text_native: Yes, the same. We'll know who you are.

panels.visual_direction: Medium close on Margaux as she wipes a glass and looks at the learner; Gus leans forward from the booth, theatrical. Romy listens, pen ready.
panels.alt_native: Margaux asks the learner 'La même chose ?' while Gus speaks from the booth.

panels.narration_fr: Tout le monde attend votre réponse.
panels.visual_direction: Close-up on Lila smiling, then looking curious; Romy tilts her head toward the learner as if offering the microphone of attention to them.
panels.alt_native: Lila asks why the learner stays; Romy asks if it's because of the inheritance.

panels.visual_direction: Panel with no dialogue: a hand close-up of Margaux sliding a saucer across the zinc; the rain streaks the window behind it.
panels.alt_native: Margaux slides a saucer across the bar; rain on the window.

draft.suggested_response_fr: Je prends un café-crème, parce que je reste pour régler la succession d'Odile.
draft.hint_native: Say one café order (e.g. 'un café-crème') and then give a short reason: 'parce que...' Mention you are staying to handle the succession or papers.
draft.translation_native: The same as usual? / I will have a café-crème, because I am staying to sort out Odile's succession.

season_checklist.change_before: Le Mistral ne connaît pas encore votre commande habituelle.
season_checklist.change_after: Votre commande devient votre 'habitude' reconnue au café.
season_checklist.turn_want: Choose your order and say why you remain in Paris.
season_checklist.hook_fr: À suivre… Gus a quelque chose à annoncer.
season_checklist.complication: Tomorrow, someone will mention Solvel's letter left in the stairwell, making the question of why you stay suddenly more urgent.

refusals.hint: The narration addresses the learner as "vous" while the character speaks to them as "tu". Pick one and use it everywhere: switching between tu and vous inside a scene reads as a mistake to a learner who is being taught the difference.
